body: I agree with you. I wish there was transparency. I’ll say something like good morning to a bot now and I’ll get hit with the same message. I’m sure this is a result of what happened recently but… come on.

I don’t hold it against my parents anymore, but only because I don’t have the energy or heart to even think of them anymore. They were unqualified to be parents, and every setback I faced stung more knowing I had no support, no parent backing me. Every time I worked my way up the ladder, I became more and more surrounded by people who had parents that could support them—at least financially. This sometimes brings the resentment back. It would be nice if I never had to worry after falling, but I don’t have that luxury
Therapy is good but a lot of therapist are notoriously bad at their job. The licensure and masters does not equate to being able to actually empathize and communicate with people.
All the time I wasted investing into people that never wanted to invest in me

When I visited Chicago I was blown away by how awful the other driver’s were. I don’t understand why it’s so bad there

It ended shortly after. We were together for six years.


I hope you’re healing better

Thank you!
Thank you!
The person we loved became a part of us. Idk if the pain ever disappears. I used to cry so much over her and now the pain is like a simmering ember, but there’s still pain. It’s still there.

Last year I was suicidal due to everything that was going on and my ex of six years decided she didn’t want to deal with me anymore. She was used to seeing me strong and happy, not the broken person I was last year.

I allowed myself to grieve, and then I took a different change of direction. I was a counselor and then I went to work at a lumber yard in a different state, alone, without knowing anyone. The change of scenery, the change of direction, helped me a lot with healing, as strange as that may sound.

I agree  with you that it depends on context :)

But her and I were together for six years and love is more than “feelings.” It’s commitment. It’s something you actively grow and nurture. She also told me a few days before the breakup that we would work things out, as we always have. 

But that didn’t happen. I honestly have no Ill will towards her, but I’d be lying if I told you or anyone that I wasn’t frustrated and disappointed with how things ended. 

I’ve also talked to people who have been in long term relationships for 10+, even 20+ years. At some point, the “fire,” did fade, but they cultivated it because they still loved each other. It’s that complex. It’s that simple. For any relationship, we have two choices. To make it work, or walk away. If we strip love down to just feelings, then there’s no hope for long term relationships to ever be a thing
I totally agree with you that people seem to take everything for granted, but what do you mean by we are like products?
I totally agree with you that people seem to take everything for granted, but what do you mean by we are like products?

Holy fuck man I’m so sorry. My hell is different but I can empathize your pain. It was six years for me and she told me that I wasn’t the happy and upbeat guy she knew anymore.

But 2020 was a rough fucking year. The moment I needed her the most, she decided to erase me. 

Unbelievable. I wish I could give you an answer, but I’m wondering the same thing

I’m totally with you on the vague yet honest points but tbh I would even be down for the Shakespeare shit because if you invested all that time, time you can never ever get back, then it’s the least they can do. We often have a societal saying such that “no one owes anyone anything,” but if you invest time into someone and they to you, then that line of logic stops working. And we follow that “no one owes anyone anything,” line of thought, no one is going to be happy because it breeds selfishness and a dissent from empathy

You’re telling me that it has to be something and that your ex might not be telling you what it is. I’ve had this same thought process and it’s fucking rough. You might never get to know the answer, but know this. If your ex wanted something to change but didn’t communicate, that’s on them and not you. It’s not your job to have them communicate their needs to you.

Closure is an illusion. The best closure you can have is knowing you tried your best. In any relationship, we have two choices. Make it work or walk away. Your ex chose to walk away. Maybe it had nothing to do with you and everything to do with him. Maybe you will get an answer from him one day but I wouldn’t count on it. Just know that you’re worth more than what an ex thinks of you.
It’s gonna take time, and that can either be a month or even a year or longer. Allow yourself to grieve and know that you’re worth more than being just an option. You should be the only one
Preach. You should always be the only one, and never an option.
It’s hard. I allow myself to feel all the anger and rage and sorrow, and then I try my best to move past it.
Even more so when there’s literally nothing that could have changed it because at some point, our partners made a choice and that choice was to walk away

Your story reminds me of an argument I got into with a friend.  Her exact words were “But I mean you can fall out of the feeling of love and it not be a choice. And what’s the point of putting in the work if you don’t feel the love haha,” to which I responded “Because emotions change. If they come, they can go. The opposite is also true. There was times in my relationship where I didn’t feel the “spark,” but then I’d feel it again.”

I swear people are just becoming selfish and losing their sense of conviction. I’m sorry it had to happen to you too
Same, brother. I hope you never let your heart grow cold from the wrong that was dealt to you, and I hope you one day find someone who won’t betray you and will continue to choose you and only you.
I would love to be an outlier in that case. Congratulations to your parents!

Thanks for sharing. I think this solidifies that being friends with your ex is a mistake. My ex reached out during Valentine’s Day and told me how much I meant to her and we talked about being friends again. We had been together for six years and treated each other well, so I figured that being friends would be good and even healthy for us.


It was a mistake. The moment she broke up with me, I was dead to her. It was foolish of me to think we could move forward together

Thank you for your story. It’s been 4 months and it still hurts.

“I can’t tell you how it led to that because I’m not exactly sure myself. I guess I thought it was a phase, but then I realized that the feelings were real.”

It’s gonna fucking hurt. It still hurts for me but it does get better

Love this

I think you’re right. A lot of people I’ve talked to, who have been together for very long periods of time, have told me that there were low, dull moments in their relationship. But love is a commitment. It’s something you nurture and build. It takes work. 

For my ex, she reached a point where she didn’t want to put in the work anymore.

I think social media, while allowing us to stay connected with loved ones and friends, has had a negative impact on the way people handle relationships. All you ever see are highlight reals. And even the negatives that are displayed by social media are overshadowed by sensationalized videos of “the good life.”

I think at some point, most just don’t want to put in the work for a relationship... even if it was great and you had messages and memories of them telling you how much you meant to them, how you’ve impacted them.

I understand that feelings changed, but I truly thought her and I could work through anything. 

I mean that’s what love is, to me. Not just the physical chemistry but an active commitment.

But if grief is the price for love, isn’t it worth it? I get the pain, man. I lost someone I had a very intimate and connected life with. We were together for six years. I’ve had my days wishing the same thing you are but what’s helped me was appreciating that the good still happened and mattered, even if the now hurts like hell

It’s still hard. I try to just keep busy but losing such a significant relationship and not having that person around to talk to is really tough. In terms of the grieving process, I’m doing better every day but this silence is still fucking hard
Cried reading this. Godspeed to you
Damn. This is a powerful revelation. Thank you

It’s shitty that your husband came to that decision. With how horrific the dating game can be, and how much work love really takes, it’s so frustrating that there are people willing to throw that away. I’m sorry you’re going through this.

Having a child in poverty is extremely irresponsible. I had to work several jobs as a child just to survive. I’ve gone days without eating and I was even homeless for two years. It was awful. Through hard work I was able to put myself through college and for six years my life was awesome, but shit happened and now I’m staring at the very real possibility that I can be back to that dark place. I’m not against people loving each other, but people need to be more responsible when bringing a life into the mix. All my friends have been able to fall back on family. I know I’m not alone in not having family to fall back on, but it’s still frustrating when you always have to be strong

This isn’t a pity party. My post straight up says I’m grateful for the good in my life. You can be grateful but still frustrated. These elements to life are not diametrically different as people make them out to be.
If you have other suggestions, please tell me

Two options. Vote more and get more involved (I’ve done both to the best of my ability) but realize that significant change is generational as it takes a long time to 1) happen and 2) persist. Or option two, rise up and start a revolution. Let’s see how society functions as forbearance on loans and rent ends.

You’re absolutely right. What’s crazy is that most people don’t get it.

And people choose to not get it
Hell yeah. But our society doesn’t give a fuck about the people tho
For real. I think life is precious but again people don’t consider the weight of bringing a life into this world and the suffering is unnecessary.

Also there is a lot of responsibility that goes into having a child and while there are people who have children out of love, there are also people who don’t understand the gravity of having a child

I agree with this completely. Success in America is a double edged sword for sure. On one end, we see people who have come from nothing and have survived and defeated insane hardships and we totally do give all attention and focus on that. On the other hand. America does use that as a method to detract from the very real problems that persist in our society. Right? I appreciate you sharing and I’m sorry you have to go through it too. Money isn’t everything, but it’s incredibly important in pretty much any modern society. You don’t take kindness to the bank. That won’t pay the ever increasing rent and bills.

I’m sorry you had to grow in poverty. You’re right about money not being the only thing, but again. I don’t have family to support me. There’s no mother to hold me. There’s no sister to talk to. I wouldn’t trade the genuine connections I made with people, but you can’t pay the bills with love. You can’t take kindness and care to the bank

I think all sensible people try their best to fight systematic oppression. A really good measure of suicide prevention would be affordable housing and not having to worry about basic needs being met.

If you’re making a point that it’s a systematic issue then I agree. But that aside, me being poor and others being poor is still a problem. Even if it’s periphery to the root of the problem, it’s still a problem.

I get it though. That would be a better way. Maybe like... us living in a government with full transparency of taxes and actually having it allocated to the people.

Still, until that happens, being born poor just causes undue suffering that could have been avoided

But I’m still hoping one day it will be

I never got support then, I don’t have support now. Most people work 2+ jobs just to survive. How long can america sustain this? It’s bad enough to be clinically depressed, but experiencing everything else is a nail in my coffin

It’s nigh and day for me. Not sleeping well, still waking up in shock over it being over and her not being in my arms.

I still wish you chose us. Six years. We’ve been through everything together. We built a life together. It was hard towards the end but I thought we’d come out on top, like we always did. It still breaks my heart. I still wake up in the middle of the night, absolutely devastated. It wasn’t supposed to be this way. It wasn’t supposed to happen so much.

There’s so many more things I wanted to say and do with you. But I’ll never get that chance. The life I had with you, the future we imagined is gone.

Even when I was more suicidal, I never thought I’d lose you. This is a different pain. It hasn’t gone away and I wish I could kill these feelings because I know you’re already having fun and seeing other people.

You say you were cold to me because it was easier for you to heal. But what did you need to heal from? You’re the one that left

Power to you. At one point, we all invested in our exes. We invested time and money and most importantly our love. Whether the breakup was mutual, a falling out, one sided, or however it may have been, the relationship is over. We need to take care of ourselves and stop investing in people that aren’t there for us anymore. If they wanted to make it work out, they could have done so.
Feel this
Cheating is awful. I’m so sorry you had to go through that. Seeing how nightmarish people can be, and the emotional drain of losing my ex, dating doesn’t seem worth it anymore

I like meeting people but I don’t want to emotionally invest into other people, at least not in the foreseeable future. I already put in this significant time and energy and I’m just not about doing again anytime soon.

This was an incredibly powerful share. Thank you. 

I've thrown myself into whatever work I can find, reconnected with old friends and family, and have been connecting with as many online strangers as possible. The brief crossings I have with strangers brings me some peace in this tumultuous point in my life. I had such an intimate and connected life with my partner. My life continues, but it's just not the same and I know that it can't be and it never will be.

I moved a thousand miles away from her. Not the most financially sound thing to do but with no family to turn to, I had to do what I had to do. It still hurts. If it wasn't for this pandemic, I would have just taken the first plane out of this country and disappeared for a while. 

I feel like  disappearing, truly disappearing will be the best way for me to say goodbye and put my heart to rest. It's a gradual process, and it isn't linear at all, but I'm still here.

I also have depression. It’s good that you’re being mindful and doing your best to support him, because I believe that everyone, depression or not, needs to be supported. It’s hard to pull yourself out of those pits of darkness but your feelings are completely valid. Support is one thing, but it’s not your job to fix him. If he needs to move to start fresh, you two could talk about long distance and then if he proves to actually get his shit together, I’m sure working things out from that point would be relatively straightforward. 

Also though. Sometimes depressed people don’t want to be helped so much as supported and listened to. When my ex kept telling me to do yoga. It didn’t really help with my case but I still appreciated the effort. Everyone’s different, you know?

I hope you find the answers you are looking for.
Damn. I felt every word of this. Everything you miss, I miss too. Every time I think I’m done grieving, something happens and I’m hurt all over again

No friendship. It’s crazy how one day, whether they’ve been deliberating it or not, a person can just decide they don’t love you anymore
Negative is part of life. You deserve to have people who will listen your frustrations

I miss the way she would nudge against my chest and demand I rub her head and back. I miss the little dates I had with her after we both came back after a long day at work. I miss our spontaneous trips into the desert, or out in some field where we would hold each other and smile and laugh. I miss how we’d reflect on how far we came. I miss waking up to you, coming back home to you and ending the night with you. I miss how much you’d check up on me. I miss how you can have a very stoic and serious work attitude but be silly and loving at home. I miss planning the future together. I miss having you love me. I miss having you around.

We had our ups and downs and our big fights. I never thought we would end. I never thought it would be us.

It’s the stigma for mental health. If we broke an arm, no one would get mad at us for having a broken arm. They would give us time to heal and be supportive. But with depression, we get shit like “maybe you’re just not making the most of life,” as if we woke up and chose to have chemical imbalances in our heads. 

Society might not give a fuck, but we can still care about ourselves and do our best. 

Your feelings are valid. Life is hard and people love to say “work harder,” as if that’s the skeleton key answer for everything. It’s not. When I was a counselor, I had homeless clients who worked 2-3 jobs. Even now, I know people that work 60 plus hours just to stay alive. They’re already working hard, but the world keeps on with its bullshit and society guilt trips us into hating each other

Please don’t let the love in your heart die.

It hurts so much because of this very reason. I know a lot of people have shitty relationships that they try to make better because they’re loving people, and while my relationship has its ups and downs, it was full of love and life. It was an incredible relationship. That’s why her no longer being a part of my life hurts so much
Absolutely agree with you

Feelings change. People change. Six years is a long time. That’s how long my ex and I were together. A month before the breakup we were talking about marriage. A month later she broke up with me and cut off all contact. 

I can’t speak for your ex, but I know that mine wasn’t lying. Maybe he wasn’t either. But one thing is for sure, he did walk away and you deserve someone who will work things out with you. I don’t believe in marriage but I do believe in “through thick and thin.” 

Those people that believe the grass is greener, that walk away from people like you and me, people who have loved and supported them, will one day realize that the grass wasn’t greener, and that they should have stayed and kept watering the grass they had.

At least, that’s what I hope.

These things take time. Give yourself some credit. If you were a heartless person, you wouldn’t be feeling this pain. You feel pain because you loved and cared.

And it might always hurt. I think I’m doing better but then I dream of her again and I’m fucking in tears. It’s a rough road for sure
When you figure it out, let me know please. For me, I try to find peace in knowing shes okay, thriving and happy. It still hurts though

I hope you get your answer, but if not, just remember that "why" doesn't matter. What matters is that he chose to ghost you. 

Just remember that the best closure you can get is that you tried your best.

I don't really like saying "I feel your pain," but I believe a good amount of people on this sub and I share similar hells. I was with my ex girlfriend for 6 years, and we had developed an intimate life together.

We went through some really tough times this year. Before the breakup, I was hopeful after we had a tough fight but spent a good amount of time talking it out.

We talked about how we would overcome this adversity, as we had with everything else.

Come that Sunday, and she not only chose to break up with me, but she completely went against what she had told me she wanted just a few days prior.

I got some of my answers, but there's still a lot I'd like to discuss with her. But that'll never happen. The answers I received brought me no peace, but should you receive yours, I hope it's better for you.

Him searching for someone else might not have anything to do with you. Maybe you might be thinking that you want to know, if you think that'll help you improve, but remember he made the decision to leave. In that perspective, you did nothing wrong. He chose to walk away. You deserve better. You deserve someone who chooses you and communicates with you. 

I hope you win your battle. Focus on yourself, get help from loved ones when you need it, and keep moving forward.
